title: POC Network Rehearsal & Routing Acceptance — AstraVault
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on a dry-run cutover (rehearsal) of Redwood Private into AstraVault VPC, validation of routing acceptance criteria, and review of kernel and quantization upgrade impact. Agreed on go/no-go checklist items, some outstanding MTU/egress shaping tweaks, and follow-ups for security artifacts.
topics: Routing acceptance criteria and rollback triggers
VPC egress shaping and MTU mismatch troubleshooting
Security audit docs and KMS integration sign-off
Next steps for final acceptance test
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: All right folks thanks for joining on time. Quick roll call — me, Diego from infra, Sara on CSM side.
[00:08] Maya Singh: Maya here, Jon, Priya and Ethan also on.
[00:12] Lena Park: Great. Agenda today: run the rehearsal checklist, validate routing acceptance, and confirm kernel/quant schedule. We'll try and keep to 45 minutes.
[00:25] Diego Marin: I'll start with the routing diff — we ran the staging sweep this morning, most flows hit the private gateway, fallback path to hosted tier exercised twice. There was a ~20ms spike on the long tail when KV cache warmed.
[00:40] Jon Ruiz: That spike was the one we noticed yesterday — it correlated with the batch job that bursts traffic. How deterministic is that?
[00:48] Diego Marin: It's workload dependent; continuous batching hesitates on cold KV. We saw it consistently at around t+3s for sequences over 1k tokens in our synthetic tests.
[00:58] Ethan Cole: For the rehearsal we need to confirm the BGP adjacency doesn't flap when we switch rtr-1 to the private path. Last time we saw a route withdrawal for ~6s.
[01:08] Sara O'Neill: Noted — that's in the checklist under routing stability.
[01:12] Priya Desai: On security, quick reminder we still need final sign-off on KMS integration and encryption at rest proofs — the SOC/ISO artifacts Diego sent were good but we need the HSM integration diagram.
[01:22] Diego Marin: I'll drop the HSM diagram after this call, yeah.
[01:25] Lena Park: Perfect. OK, run the rehearsal step-by-step: step 1 pre-cutover validation, step 2 switch traffic, step 3 monitor fallbacks, step 4 rollback. Maya, you leading the cutover side?
[01:36] Maya Singh: Yes I will coordinate. We propose to do the dry-run Saturday 02:00 AM UTC to minimize user impact.
[01:45] Jon Ruiz: Weekend window is fine. We want two independent observers on routing and two on telemetry.
[01:51] Ethan Cole: On MTU — still seeing occasional PMTU blackholes for jumbo frames when the onboarded CNIs set 9000. Our workaround was to set 1500 on the private tunnel.
[02:03] Diego Marin: The runtime tries to use large pages and that can expose MTU mismatches; setting 1500 in the tunnel reduced retransmits by ~12% in the lab.
[02:13] Priya Desai: We need that documented in the runbook so auditors know we intentionally set tunnel MTU.
[02:18] Lena Park: We'll add an explicit MTU section. Next, kernel and quantization upgrade — Diego?
[02:25] Diego Marin: We're proposing to push the optimized kernels (v2.4) and the 4-bit quant profile in a canary on one pod per rack. Perf improved ~18% p50 latency, token cost down ~11% in our bench. But there are a couple of edge cases with verbs and the older drivers.
[02:42] Maya Singh: Which drivers? We're on 520.x series on production boxes.
[02:46] Diego Marin: If you're on 520.x you should be fine for kernel update, but the quant paths require a small patch to the network driver for RDMA fallback. That patch will be in the release notes.
[02:56] Jon Ruiz: We can't ship that patch without sign-off from infra and security — need a CVE scan and test matrix.
[03:04] Diego Marin: Understood. We'll attach the CVE results to the change ticket and snapshot the canary test results.
[03:10] Lena Park: Back to routing acceptance criteria: recall the list we agreed — sustained p99 < 250ms for the private path, no route withdrawal > 2s, and graceful fallback under overload to hosted model under 5% error amplification.
[03:23] Maya Singh: Those numbers still work for us. We need to confirm the telemetry dashboard will flag p99 breaches and automatically trigger the rollback policy.
[03:31] Sara O'Neill: The console alerting rule is in staging; we can mirror it to the customer's telemetry via the webhook.
[03:37] Ethan Cole: I want to run a simulated failover where we drop one rack and confirm KV cache invalidation behavior. Last time cache cold start caused 30% latency tail.
[03:47] Diego Marin: We'll run a controlled rack fail at the dry-run and observe the cache warm-up window. For the rehearsal we'll also pre-warm frequently used prefixes to reduce the tail.
[03:56] Jon Ruiz: Can you pre-warm from our real prefix lists? We can give you a sanitized set.
[03:59] Diego Marin: Yes please send the prefix list.
[04:02] Priya Desai: Also need to verify audit logs are preserved and shipped to your SIEM during the cutover; ensure no log gaps.
[04:09] Sara O'Neill: We've done end-to-end checks in staging; we'll do a retention smoke test during the rehearsal.
[04:14] Lena Park: Good. Any concerns around procurement or contract gating for Saturday?
[04:18] Maya Singh: No procurement gating. We do need an updated IP allowlist for the Redwood maintenance windows — Ethan will post the final IP block.
[04:25] Ethan Cole: Will do after the call.
[04:28] (brief crosstalk)
[04:32] Diego Marin: Quick note — we observed an egress shaping policy that can throttle bursts; it's set conservatively in your VPC. For cutover we recommend a temporary increase to the burst window for 20 minutes to allow cache warm.
[04:46] Jon Ruiz: That feels risky for other downstream systems, can it be scoped just to inference egress CIDR?
[04:53] Diego Marin: Yes we can request a scoped exception so it only affects the inference endpoints.
[04:58] Priya Desai: Scoped exception must be in writing and timeboxed.
[05:02] Lena Park: We'll provide the scoped exception language and the exact time window in an email.
[05:07] Maya Singh: On rollback triggers, please reiterate the thresholds — we'll do automated rollback if p99 > 300ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows or route withdrawal > 2s.
[05:19] Diego Marin: Confirmed. We'll keep a human in the loop during the first five minutes after switch.
[05:24] Sara O'Neill: I'll be on the bridge to coordinate and post the timeline steps to the channel.
[05:28] Lena Park: Excellent. Any last open items?
[05:31] Jon Ruiz: We need bench numbers once the kernel/quant canary runs — specifically p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta.
[05:38] Diego Marin: We'll publish a canary report and include comparison charts.
[05:42] Maya Singh: Also want a short rehearsal runbook (1-page) for the on-call team.
[05:47] Lena Park: We'll prepare a 1-page runbook and the full playbook.
[05:50] (pause)
[05:55] Priya Desai: Security question — does Redwood keep a separate key in KMS per tenant or a shared envelope key? We need per-tenant separation.
[06:03] Diego Marin: We do per-tenant CMKs by default for Private deployments; the HSM integration diagram will show the envelope flow.
[06:09] Priya Desai: OK please attach the diagram and the HSM cert chain.
[06:14] Lena Park: Action items we will capture. Quick timeline recap: rehearsal Saturday 02:00 UTC, kernel canary to run Friday 18:00 UTC, deliver HSM diagram today, scoped egress exception request by Ethan.
[06:29] Maya Singh: Sounds good. We'll invite two netops observers and two telemetry observers.
[06:34] Lena Park: Great, next meeting — post-rehearsal readout Monday morning, same time.
[06:40] Jon Ruiz: One more small ask — can Redwood run an A/B compare for model latency on both quant and non-quant images during canary?
[06:48] Diego Marin: Yes we'll instrument and produce side-by-side distribution plots.
[06:52] Lena Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the checklist and the scoped exception language.
[06:58] (meeting ends)
